summary: Alberta Wildfire steel lookout tower, about 30 m, constructed 2012 per the provincial database, reached by air; no earlier history or staffing record found.

access.note: The public is forbidden to climb lookout towers and lookout dwellings are for private use (Alberta's general rules for lookout sites); the provincial database lists access mode as fly. No site-specific closure notice was found.

events.note: Database field Year Constructed. The sources read do not say whether an earlier structure stood on the site.

sources.title: Wildfire lookout record for Sandy Lake (WF_WILDFIRE_LOOKOUT, FRIAA FireSmart vector data)

notes_for_editor: Thin record. Site facts come from one provincial database row (FRIAA WF_WILDFIRE_LOOKOUT, NAME SANDY LAKE); YEAR_CONSTRUCTED is the database's construction year; the sources do not say whether this was the first tower on the site. The database gives ACCESS_MODE fly (air access), so no drive-up visit is recorded. Two searches and the reads found no history, staffing, fire or site-condition record for this lookout. Search results on 'Sandy Lake' returned news of a May 2026 wildfire at a Sandy Lake near Sandy Beach, which the search did not tie to this tower, so it was not used. Brief's access 'closed' is kept: the sources support it only through Alberta's general rules for lookout sites, not a site notice, so an editor may want to confirm the level. Brief's height, elevation, lat/lon and 2012 build year all match the database row. Rights caution: the FRIAA layer description classifies the dataset as 'Protected' and says its features are 'not to be displayed on maps with a scale larger than 1:1,000,000 or on maps that show local roads, that are going to be seen by the general public'. Check that before this lookout's location appears on a public map. Alberta's page says 100 active lookout sites; an older open.alberta.ca map (metadata dated 2009) says 127. The story uses neither count.
